idiom_name: amqplib publish options / KafkaJS record headers
implementation_notes: The Node messaging clients ship the envelope: amqplib's channel.publish takes the payload as a Buffer plus a properties object (contentType, contentEncoding, headers, correlationId, replyTo, messageId, timestamp, type, appId) and the consumer receives them back as msg.properties, while a Kafka record carries key/value plus an explicit headers map. The classic wrapper class is therefore replaced by the client library's property bag: build the metadata object at the outbound adapter and give application code only msg.content or record.value. Wrap the payload inside the body yourself only when the channel does not carry the required fields.
pitfalls: msg.content is a Buffer view whose memory is only valid during the callback; retain a copy or the decoded string, not the Buffer, if the payload outlives the handler.
AMQP header values are typed (string, number, boolean, timestamp) and arrive in client-specific shapes - never assume a header is a string.
Re-publishing a received message with a fresh properties object silently drops the original headers unless they are copied explicitly.
